title: PRD Addendum: Model Ingest Policy for Edge-Case Open Weights (soft-pins & compatibility heuristics)
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket is an addendum to the model catalog PRD focused on onboarding unusual or edge-case open weights (eg. forked checkpoints, mixed-format checkpoints, experimental quantized weights) where standard compatibility assertions are insufficient. The goal is to define operational acceptance criteria, a lightweight compatibility heuristic, soft-pinning semantics, and an automated sanity probe suite that enables safe staged admission into the hosted catalog without compromising runtime stability or SLA targets. This work bridges PM acceptance requirements and ENG integration tasks for the intake pipeline and runtime feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: A compact compatibility heuristic (CSV/JSON) exists and is generated for every ingest that flags: architecture, expected kv-cache behavior, tokenization variant, known quantization format, expected memory footprint, and required kernel features.
Soft-pin policy documented: soft-pinned variants may be routed to dedicated validation pools for 7 days; production routing only after passing sanity probes or manual PM sign-off.

Automated runtime sanity probe suite (3 probes) runs on the validation pool: cold start generation, long-context kv-cache stability (>= 2k tokens), and a deterministic output regression check against a small eval set; probes must pass with zero crashes and within defined latency thresholds.
Intake UI shows compatibility flags and the soft-pin status; API exposes pinLevel: [unverified, soft-pinned, pinned].
Rollback criteria defined: fail probe X times or observe >0.5% server errors in validation pool => automatic unpublish and alert to on-call.
Documentation (Confluence) links created that explain pin semantics, escalation path, and customer-facing messaging templates.
ENG implementation tasks created for the runtime feature gating and the validation pool; unit/integration tests present in PR.
Security review completed for variants that require KMS/HSM key access or include provenance metadata that triggers PII inspection.
Metrics dashboards updated: per-variant error rate, validation-pool latency, and pin-transition audit log entries are visible in Console by default.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: PM/Eng alignment — acceptance criteria should err on conservative side to protect SLA; agreed to soft-pin 7-day validation window (Maya, Arjun, Priya).

open_questions: What is the minimum probe pass rate to allow soft-pinned variants to be promoted automatically? (proposal: 100% pass across probe suite for 3 consecutive runs)
Should we allow customers to opt-out of soft-pin validation and take full responsibility? (legal/contract implications)
How to represent compatibility confidence in the SDK responses without cluttering telemetry?
Cost allocation: validation pool GPU hours — charge to model owner or absorbed by catalog budget?
notes: Trade-offs: strict pre-admission gating reduces incidents but slows time-to-availability for community models; soft-pins try to balance speed and safety.
Operational playbook: on publish failure alert -> automatic unpublish -> create incident ticket with prefilled diagnostics bundle.
We will monitor for false-positives in the heuristic in the first 30 days and iterate on fields to reduce manual review load.
If validation-pool costs grow >15% month-over-month, revisit economic model and consider charging model owners for validation runs.
